For example, the 99% species protection DGV for BPA could be applied to a slightly-to-moderately disturbed ecosystem.

table_or_page: master table worksheet "Sheet1", row 163, column G
note: published 2026 | The DGVs supersede the ANZECC/ARMCANZ (2000) DGVs for Copper in freshwater. The DGVs apply to dissolved copper (i.e. < 0.45 µm filtered measurement) in freshwater with a dissolved organic carbon concentration (DOC) of ≤0.5 mg/L. The DGVs can be adjusted for different DOC concentrations to produce bioavailability adjusted guideline values (BAGVs), within the following hardness and pH ranges: hardness between 2 mg/L and 400 mg/L as CaCO3 and pH between 6.0 and 8.5. The DGVs at 0.5 mg/L DOC may be close to analytical detection limits routinely used by commercial laboratories (e.g. 1 µg/L); however, when DOC is 1 mg/L or more, the associated BAGVs are likely to be above typical limits of detection. The Water Quality Guidelines provide advice on cases where the DGV is less than the limit of detection. See the copper in freshwater DGV technical brief for further details. The DGVs and the information in the corresponding DGVs technical brief for this toxicant should be used in accordance with the detailed guidance provided on the Australian and New Zealand Guidelines for Fresh and Marine Water Quality website. This includes the use of the tiered assessment framework[RvD1.1] for dissolved copper in freshwater.
